verdict_reason: pyMack first-mode neutral frequency (temporal, c_i=0, L* scale, condition=table_11_1) vs Mack's digitized 'complete' curve, M=2.2. Best-matching branch = 'peak': median |dF|/F = 68% over 11 R in [200,1600] (>15% -> disagrees). All branches: lower 101% (10 pts), upper 166% (10 pts), peak 68% (11 pts). Critical-R / topology gap: Mack's curve is unstable down to R=90, but pyMack's first mode is STABLE below R~300 (only 73% of the digitized R range is covered by an unstable pyMack band). pyMack's neutral frequencies are systematically too HIGH (~2x the Mack curve) and the band decays differently with R. CONVERGENCE-CHECKED: mode selection is the continuous c_r~0.4-0.51 first mode (not a spurious low-c_r root); the alpha scan brackets both neutral crossings; and y_max is generous (delta*/L*~3.7, y_max=30 ~8x delta*). y_max 30->45 shifts the verdict-region (R=800) frequencies only ~11-13% and the disagreement persists at the better-converged y_max=45 (M1.6 R=800: upF 19% high, peakF 17% low), so this is convergence-stable physics -- the repo's documented low-Mach first-mode under-amplification / too-high critical Reynolds number, not a numerical artifact. Verdict 'disagrees'.

R grid 200-1600. Parallel across cores (single-thread BLAS). y_max=30->45 spot-checks at R=800 recorded for convergence (see metrics.ymax_sensitivity_R800_pct and verdict_reason).
